source: Research compilation of mid-size (12-50B) LLM decode speeds on Apple Silicon, 2026-11-21: oMLX Community Benchmarks (omlx.ai/benchmarks/performance) per chip and GPU-core bin medians at 1k-token context (tok_s_robust = median of the runs within 0.7 to 1.3 times the bin median, after a tier-aware ceiling filter; rows flagged suspect deviate by more than 40% from the same-tier bandwidth-scaled median), the llama.cpp gpt-oss guide discussion #15396 (llama-bench tg128), Jeff Geerling ai-benchmarks issue #42 (M3 Ultra, peak power), Tom's Hardware (M5 Ultra, cited but not used) and single-machine readings. Only oMLX sets with eight or more chips are kept.

sets.notes: Crowd-sourced; one row per chip+GPU-core bin. tok_s = plain median, tok_s_robust = median of runs within 0.7-1.3x the bin median (recommended; trims both throttled and speculative-decoding outliers); rows with "suspect": true deviate >40% from the same-tier bandwidth-scaled median. Detail pages checked for 114 of 601 runs (sample: ~3 runs nearest each bin median + the bin max); excluded 4 run(s) with MTP/DFlash/SpecPrefill/TurboQuant or non-Nominal thermal, and 0 run(s) whose tok/s per GB/s of rated bandwidth exceeded 1.6x the median of the same tier (base/Pro/Max/Ultra) for this model (implausible for plain decode); examples: [('M5 Pro (16c)', '82.5', 'thermal Heavy'), ('M5 Pro (20c)', '80.8', 'accel Context: Code (Python) | TurboQuant KV 6-bit | Lightning MTP'), ('M5 Pro (20c)', '80.9', 'accel Context: Code (Python) | TurboQuant KV 6-bit'), ('M2 (10c)', '28.0', 'accel Context: Code (Python) | TurboQuant KV 3-bit')]. Chassis (MacBook vs desktop) not reported. Raw per-run rows: llm_mid_omlx_raw.json.
